import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

The [`apps/`](https://github.com/calimero-network/core/tree/master/apps)
directory is the best ground truth for writing a Calimero app: every example is
a real crate. A wasmer app builds to WASM with
[`cargo mero build`](/build/cargo-mero/) and has a native
[`TestHost`](/build/quickstart/) test suite under `tests/` or in a
`#[cfg(test)]` module; a component app (marked "on the component SDK") builds
to a `wasm32-wasip2` component with `calimero-app-build` and tests on
`TestApp` plus its `scenarios/*.json`. This page walks the ones worth reading
first.

## How to read these

Each app follows the same shape (see [SDK macros](/build/sdk-macros/)):

- A single **`#[app::state]`** struct built from [collections](/build/collections/).
- An **`#[app::logic]` impl** with an `#[app::init]` constructor, mutating
  methods, and read-only views.
- Optionally an **`#[app::event]`** enum it emits.

Start with the state struct — it tells you which collection types the app leans
on, and therefore which reads and writes are cheap. Then read the
methods to see how those collections are driven. The walkthroughs below quote
the real struct and list the real method names; open the linked `src/lib.rs` for
the full bodies.

## Pick by concept

Every user-facing example below links to its source crate and to the page that
documents the concept it teaches. The ones marked **(walkthrough below)** also
have a full worked section further down this page; the rest are compact entries —
the source is short enough to read end to end.

<Aside type="tip" title="Run the tests first">
  Every app tests without a node. A wasmer app tests natively from the repo
  root: `cargo test -p kv-store-with-handlers` (swap in any app's crate name)
  drives the methods through `TestHost`. A component app (its own `[workspace]`,
  such as `apps/kv-store`) runs `cargo test` in its directory, which builds the
  component and runs it on the real engine through `TestApp`. Either is the
  fastest way to see an app's behavior before installing it.
</Aside>

## kv-store

The canonical starting point, on the component SDK (`calimero-app-sdk`, built for
`wasm32-wasip2` into a `calimero:app` component): a string→string store whose
writes the app's log orders, so a later write to a key replaces an earlier one.
The wasmer build of the same store, which the node's own tests run, is
`apps/wasmer-fixtures/kv-store`.

**State shape** ([`apps/kv-store/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/calimero-network/core/tree/master/apps/kv-store/src/lib.rs)):

```rust
#[app::state(version = 1)]
pub struct KvStore {
    entries: UnorderedMap<String, String>,
}
```

An `UnorderedMap` holds values under their key in key order and keeps its own
count of keys, changed only by adding, so `len` is one read. For records with
indexes, unique constraints and counts, use a `Table` (see the
[tutorial](/build/tutorial/)).

**Key methods** (ABI names are camelCase; `u64` travels as a decimal string):

| Method | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `set { key, value }` | Insert or overwrite a key; emits `Inserted` or `Updated`. |
| `updateIfExists { key, value }` | Replace only an existing key; returns whether it did. |
| `getOrInsert { key, value }` | Read-or-create; returns the value the key holds after the call. |
| `get` / `getUnchecked` / `getResult` `{ key }` | Three read views: optional, trapping, and erroring (`NotFound { key }`). |
| `entries` | Every pair as a JSON object ordered by key. |
| `len` / `remove { key }` / `clear` | Count, delete one (`Removed`), delete all (`Cleared`). |

**Build & run.** `cargo test` in `apps/kv-store` builds the component and runs
`tests/harness.rs` and every `scenarios/*.json` on the real engine. From the repo
root, build the component and create a context from it on a development cluster:

```sh
cargo run -p calimero-app-build -- apps/kv-store --out kv_store.wasm
meroctl context create --name my-kv --path kv_store.wasm --alias my-kv
meroctl call -c my-kv set --args '{"key": "hello", "value": "world"}'
meroctl call -c my-kv get --args '{"key": "hello"}' --view
```

## kv-store-with-handlers

Same key/value core as `kv-store`, but each `set`/`remove`/`clear` emits an
event tagged with a **handler method name** — showing how an emitted event can
be routed to a callback method. It also keeps a `Counter` of handler runs.

**State shape** ([`apps/kv-store-with-handlers/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/calimero-network/core/tree/master/apps/kv-store-with-handlers/src/lib.rs)):

```rust
#[app::state(emits = for<'a> Event<'a>)]
pub struct KvStore {
    items: UnorderedMap<String, LwwRegister<String>>,
    handlers_called: UnorderedMap<String, LwwRegister<String>>,
    handler_counter: Counter,
}
```

**Key methods:**

| Method | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `set` / `remove` / `clear` | Like the wasmer `kv-store` (`apps/wasmer-fixtures/kv-store`), but `emit!` pairs the event with a handler name (e.g. `"insert_handler"`). |
| `insert_handler` / `update_handler` / `remove_handler` / `clear_handler` | The handler callbacks; each logs and bumps `handler_counter`. |
| `get_handler_execution_count()` | The number of handler runs. |
| `get_handlers_called()` / `get_unique_handlers_called()` / `was_handler_called(name)` | Introspect which handlers ran. |
| `get` / `entries` / `len` | The same reads as `kv-store`. |

<Aside type="note" title="Handlers are not auto-dispatched in TestHost">
  The native harness captures emitted events but does not run their handlers —
  the app's own tests call `insert_handler(...)` directly to exercise the
  bookkeeping. The event→handler routing happens on a node, where the app's
  leader runs each handler once after the entry commits.
</Aside>

**Build & run.** `cargo mero bundle --dev --no-icon` produces
`dist/com.calimero.kv-store-with-handlers-0.0.0.mpk`; install and call it as in
the [Quickstart](/build/quickstart/).

## collaborative-editor

A real-time collaborative text editor built on the **`ReplicatedGrowableArray`**
(RGA) text collection, so each insert or delete names its place in the text
by character id, not by an index another user's edit may have shifted.

**State shape** ([`apps/collaborative-editor/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/calimero-network/core/tree/master/apps/collaborative-editor/src/lib.rs)):

```rust
#[app::state(emits = EditorEvent)]
pub struct EditorState {
    pub document: ReplicatedGrowableArray,
    pub edit_count: Counter,
    pub metadata: UnorderedMap<String, LwwRegister<String>>,
    pub owner: Frozen<String>,
}
```

Every field is a collection, as `#[app::state]` requires. `metadata` holds
`"title"` as an LWW register any editor may change. The creating account is a
`Frozen<String>`: written once in `init`, and the storage layer refuses any
later write, so no member can rename the owner.

**Key methods:**

| Method | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `insert_text(position, text)` | Insert at an index; bumps `edit_count`, emits `TextInserted`. |
| `delete_text(start, end)` | Delete a range; emits `TextDeleted`. |
| `replace_text(start, end, text)` | Delete-then-insert in one call. |
| `append_text(text)` | Insert at the current end. |
| `clear()` | Delete the whole document. |
| `set_title(new_title)` / `get_title()` | Edit / read the `"title"` metadata register. |
| `get_text()` / `get_length()` / `is_empty()` | Read the rendered document. |
| `get_stats()` | Formatted title / length / edit-count / owner summary. |

**Build & run.** `cargo mero bundle --dev --no-icon` produces
`dist/com.calimero.collaborative-editor-0.0.0.mpk`. The collaborative payoff
appears with two members editing the same app: interleave their
`insert_text` / `delete_text` calls and read `get_text()` as each; see
[Quickstart](/build/quickstart/) for the install flow.

## team-metrics

A component-SDK app that keeps a `TeamStats` value per team in a map (wins,
losses, draws and a badge bitmask) and shows what v1's merge code becomes when one Raft
log orders every call. In v1 two apps showed this: one derived `Mergeable` for a
struct of `Counter`s, the other hand-wrote a merge (`badges |= other.badges`).
For the v1 SDK's derive and a hand-written impl, see
[SDK macros](/build/sdk-macros/) and [Advanced SDK](/build/advanced-sdk/).

**State shape** ([`apps/team-metrics/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/calimero-network/core/tree/master/apps/team-metrics/src/lib.rs)):

```rust
#[derive(Default, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct TeamStats {
    pub wins: u64,
    pub losses: u64,
    pub draws: u64,
    /// Achievement bitmask, one bit per badge (0-63).
    pub badges: u64,
}

#[app::state(version = 1)]
pub struct TeamMetricsApp {
    teams: UnorderedMap<String, TeamStats>,
}
```

A record call reads the team's value (or starts one at zero), adds one, and
writes it back; two members recording a win at once are two entries in the log,
each adding one, so there is nothing to merge. `award_badge` ORs a bit into the
current mask, so two concurrent awards both land without a merge rule.

**Key methods** (ABI names are camelCase; `u64` travels as a decimal string):

| Method | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `recordWin { teamId }` / `recordLoss` / `recordDraw` | Add one to the matching count, return the new total, emit `WinRecorded` / `LossRecorded` / `DrawRecorded`. |
| `getWins { teamId }` / `getLosses` / `getDraws` | Read a team's count; `TeamNotFound { teamId }` before its first record. |
| `awardBadge { teamId, badge }` / `getBadges` / `getBadgeCount` | Set bit `badge` (0-63, else `BadgeOutOfRange`) and return the mask; read the mask or how many bits it holds. |

**Build & run.** `cargo test --manifest-path apps/team-metrics/Cargo.toml`
builds the component and runs its harness tests and `scenarios/*.json`.
`cargo run -p calimero-app-build -- apps/team-metrics --out team_metrics.wasm`
builds the component to install as in [kv-store](#kv-store).

## blobs

A minimal file-sharing app: the binary lives in Calimero's **blob store**, while
the app holds only metadata records, each the uploader's own entry, keyed by a
generated file id that names the uploader. A client uploads the bytes to the
app, and registering the file **announces the blob to the app**, which marks
it in the app's state as the app's blob; a node of the cluster that lacks the
bytes fetches them from another node.

**State shape** ([`apps/blobs/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/calimero-network/core/tree/master/apps/blobs/src/lib.rs)):

```rust
#[app::state(emits = FileShareEvent)]
pub struct FileShareState {
    pub owner: Frozen<String>,
    pub files: AuthoredMap<String, FileRecord>,
}
```

`FileRecord` (id, name, `blob_id`, size, mime type, uploader, timestamp) is a
plain struct with a **hand-rolled `Mergeable`** that treats each record as one
value, written whole — a derive would have forced every field into its own
collection wrapper. `blob_id` is the SDK's
`BlobId` newtype, which serializes to a hex string over the wire. `files` is an
`AuthoredMap`, so only a record's uploader changes or deletes it, and the
`uploaded_by` a reader sees is read from the entry's owner stamp.

**Key methods:**

| Method | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `upload_file(name, blob_id, size, mime_type)` | Mint a `<uploader account>_<nonce>` id, `env::blob_announce_to_context(...)` the blob, store the record, emit `FileUploaded`. |
| `delete_file(file_id)` | Remove the caller's own metadata record (the underlying blob is not deleted), emit `FileDeleted`. |
| `get_file(id)` / `get_blob_id_hex(id)` | Fetch a record (the entry of the account the id names, with `get_by`) / just its `BlobId` for download. |
| `list_files()` / `search_files(query)` | All records / case-insensitive name search. |
| `get_total_files_size()` / `get_stats()` | Sum of file sizes / a formatted summary. |

<Aside type="note" title="The app stores metadata, not bytes">
  The file bytes are uploaded and downloaded through the blob client; this app
  only records the `BlobId` and announces it. See
  [Blobs](/build/guides/blobs/) for how the blob store and announcement work.
</Aside>

**Build & run.** `cargo mero bundle --dev --no-icon` produces
`dist/com.calimero.blobs-0.0.0.mpk`; install and call per the
[Quickstart](/build/quickstart/).

## xcall-example

A ping/pong across two contexts that demonstrates **cross-context calls** and,
crucially, the **xcall entry-point gate**: only methods marked `#[app::xcall]`
may be invoked from another context.

**State shape** ([`apps/xcall-example/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/calimero-network/core/tree/master/apps/xcall-example/src/lib.rs)):

```rust
#[app::state(emits = Event)]
pub struct XCallExample {
    counter: Counter,
    secret_counter: Counter,
}
```

`counter` is bumped by `pong` (the declared xcall entry point);
`secret_counter` is bumped by `secret`, which is deliberately *not* an xcall
entry point — an xcall targeting it is denied by the node before it runs.

**Key methods:**

| Method | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `ping(target_context)` | `env::xcall` the target's `pong`; emits `PingSent`. |
| `ping_secret(target_context)` | Ping the target's `secret`, to show the node denying a non-xcall target. |
| `pong(from_context)` *(`#[app::xcall]`)* | xcall-only: checks `env::xcall_origin()` matches `from_context`, then bumps `counter` and emits `PongReceived`. |
| `secret(from_context)` | A normal method (not xcall-able) that bumps `secret_counter`. |
| `get_counter()` / `get_secret_counter()` | Read each counter. |

<Aside type="note" title="ABI embedding is required for xcall gating">
  The node reads each method's `xcall_callable` flag from the ABI embedded in a
  custom WASM section to enforce the entry-point gate. `cargo mero build` embeds
  that ABI on every build, so xcall gating works with no extra step. See
  [Cross-context calls](/build/guides/cross-context/).
</Aside>

**Build & run.** `cargo mero bundle --dev --no-icon` produces
`dist/com.calimero.xcall-example-0.0.0.mpk` with the embedded ABI; install it
into two contexts, then `ping` one toward the other and watch `get_counter()`
move on the target. See [Quickstart](/build/quickstart/) for the install flow.

## Test & conformance fixtures

A handful of crates under [`apps/`](https://github.com/calimero-network/core/tree/master/apps)
are **harness and conformance fixtures**, not teaching examples — they exist to
exercise the node, the storage layer, or the wire formats, and read awkwardly as
app tutorials. Reach for them only when you are working on the harness or the
formats they pin down:

| Fixture | Role |
|---------|------|
| [`e2e-kv-store`](https://github.com/calimero-network/core/tree/master/apps/e2e-kv-store) | End-to-end node test fixture. |
| [`scaffolding-e2e`](https://github.com/calimero-network/core/tree/master/apps/scaffolding-e2e) | Fixture for the project-scaffolding end-to-end tests. |
| [`abi_conformance`](https://github.com/calimero-network/core/tree/master/apps/abi_conformance) | Pins the [app ABI](/build/app-abi/) format. |
| [`state-schema-conformance`](https://github.com/calimero-network/core/tree/master/apps/state-schema-conformance) | Pins the [state schema](/build/app-abi/) format. |
| [`migration-harness-example`](https://github.com/calimero-network/core/tree/master/apps/migration-harness-example) | Fixture for the migration harness. |
